note: Method: Deezer album/track searches and track lists, Apple lookups, MusicBrainz works lists, IMSLP api.php metadata; opened web pages: MusicWeb reviews (Gyrowetz CPO, Beecke Diogenes), classical-music.com reviews (Holzbauer, Gyrowetz Op. 44), Edition Silvertrust (Gyrowetz Op. 29); Presto, ProStudioMasters and Earsense could not be opened (403, certificate error). Open points. (1) Gyrowetz opus numbers: the Vienna Op. 29 set (1799) was reprinted in Paris/Offenbach as Op. 42 (Silvertrust), so IMSLP's Op. 42 Nos. 1-2 (E-flat, G; Sieber) are the Op. 29 quartets recorded by the Pleyel Quartett Köln (matched by key and four movements); the Gombart (Augsburg, 1802) Op. 42 is a different set (F, D, C minor; IMSLP's note on its Op. 42 set page says the two sets are not the same works) and is Quartetto Oceano's disc. The Trio Fortepiano sonatas Op. 14, 23, 28 may be IMSLP pages under other opus numbers (publishers numbered differently). (2) Dragonetti: the British Library calls the quintets solos arranged by Sechter, so they are skipped as arrangements; J. Feeney's discs (DNA 2009, 2010) record Nos. 11, 13, 18, 26, 31, and the owner may rule them in. (3) Giuliani: the guitar concertos (Op. 30, 36, 70) are recorded with orchestra only; Op. 102 and 103 for guitar and quartet are added from the Catemario disc. (4) Holzbauer: Notturni Nos. 2 and 3 (Jecklin) not added, scoring unconfirmed; CPO's "Quintet in G for fortepiano, flute and strings" is probably the Jecklin G major quintet. (5) Matiegka: Wikipedia lists a Grand Trio Op. 24; the five movements of the IMSLP page match Anke Dill's "Grand Trio, Op. 9", so the IMSLP entry carries no opus and Op. 24 is a separate added entry. (6) Kohaut: Sinfonia in F minor is a string-orchestra question; further lute concertos (D, B-flat, A, C, D minor) on the Profil, Challenge and Aparte discs are not on IMSLP and were not added (one-to-a-part not established); the Challenge disc's Trio in F is attributed to Haydn. (7) Schmitt: Op. 3 Nos. 3 and 6 taken from MusicBrainz work titles; MusicBrainz also lists a quartet for pianoforte, flute, violin and cello Op. 9 No. 1 (3 recordings) that I could not trace on Deezer. (8) Beecke: the five-movement G major quartet on the Diogenes disc (BEEV 127) "may not be by Beecke" and is left out. Not added: J.C.F. Bach's Trio Sonata in E minor (BR B 4, Camerata Köln), scoring unconfirmed. (9) IMSLP gives Giuliani's Op. 65 in A; all recordings say C major. The Trio Fortepiano (NCA) is assumed to play fortepiano, violin and cello. No composer in this slice is proposed for exclusion.
